title: LLM vs Deep Learning Object Counting Benchmark
summary: An experimental benchmark comparing language models and dedicated deep-learning models on visual object counting, with prediction quality, confidence, inference cost and latency analysis.
overview: Compares vision-capable LLMs with dedicated counting models on sample images from the FSC-147 dataset. The current pilot uses six selected images and nine LLMs (54 answers) and is explicitly not an evaluation of the full dataset.
capabilities: A JSON-schema LLM harness that records each answer's confidence, API-reported cost and latency, with pinned providers and no fallbacks.
Isolated local runners for deep-learning counters (CountGD, CounTX, FamNet, YOLO-World-S and CountGD++).
A multi-page website with a story and an explorer that lists every raw result file.
useCases: Deciding whether a general LLM is good enough for a counting task or a specialised model is needed.
A template for cost, latency and confidence comparisons across model families.
note: Sample images come from FSC-147 (Ranjan et al., CVPR 2021); the repository README credits the dataset and links its source.

title: Financial Sentiment Model Benchmark
summary: A comparative evaluation of language models, pretrained deep-learning models and decision models for financial sentiment classification, capturing predictions, confidence, cost and inference time.
overview: Benchmarks 30 balanced Financial PhraseBank sentences across three model families, with the inputs and a separate answer key included in the repository.
capabilities: LLM runs through a gateway with pinned providers, selectable reasoning levels and per-sentence request records.
Thirteen pretrained deep-learning classifiers (FinBERT, RoBERTa, DistilBERT, DeBERTa, BART families) run on a Colab T4 GPU with GPU-synchronised timing.
A separate runner for decision models, with its own timestamped result folders.
Outputs include label, confidence, reported cost, tokens, provider and inference time; failed rows can be repaired without changing successful ones.
useCases: Choosing between LLMs and small fine-tuned classifiers for sentiment tasks.
A reusable harness for cost, latency and accuracy comparisons.

title: Forward Deployed Engineer Learning Roadmap
summary: A structured engineering curriculum covering software development, applied AI engineering, retrieval, APIs, deployment and production engineering fundamentals.
overview: A three-course roadmap, taken in order, where each module lists topics with the tools to learn them. It ends with a capstone and a note on what was deliberately left out.
capabilities: Course 1, Engineering Foundations: programming, data and SQL, APIs and backend, and shipping code.
Course 2, Applied AI Engineering: LLM fundamentals, retrieval (RAG), agents and tool use, evals and observability.
Course 3, Forward Deployment: discovery and scoping, enterprise integration, deploying in a customer environment, ownership and handoff.
Supporting documents, including a course-mapping audit and alternative roadmap drafts.
useCases: Planning a self-study path towards customer-facing AI engineering roles.
Benchmarking an existing training programme against a published topic list.
